text: Right. Now that you know what this is and who it is for, let us lay out the three weeks properly, so you always know where you are and what is coming next.

The whole thing is built around two ideas held together. Breadth, and depth. Those pull in opposite directions, and getting the balance right is most of what makes a program like this useful rather than exhausting.

Breadth first. You are going to touch a lot of different tools. Cursor, GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex, Google Antigravity, Claude Code, OpenCode, and a few others along the way. Not because you need all of them. You almost certainly will not. But because in a real job you will meet whichever one your team already pays for, and you should never be the person who only knows one.

And you do not need to buy any of them to follow along. Most have a free tier or a trial, and where something is genuinely paid, you can simply watch that part. Nothing in this program is gated behind a subscription.

Then depth. We go deep on one thing in particular, and that is command line coding, with Claude Code above all. That is where the real professional work happens now, and weeks two and three live there almost entirely. Breadth so you recognise everything. Depth so you are genuinely good at one thing.
Now, the structure. Every day in this program is one of three kinds of day, and it is worth learning the three, because the shape of the day tells you how to watch it.

Some days are core skills. Those are the days we slow down and build the mental model. How models actually work, what context really is, why agents fail the way they do. Less clicking, more understanding. Today is one of those days.

Some days are platforms. Those are the hands on days, where we open the actual products and drive them. Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Antigravity, Claude Code. Lots of screen, lots of typing, lots of things going wrong on camera.

And some days are projects. Those are the days we build something real, end to end, that you could show someone. Every project in this program is a commercial project, something with actual value, except for the one we did today, which was purely for fun.
So that is three kinds of day, across three weeks, five days each. And each week has a name that tells you what changes.

Week one is vibe coding, for fun and profit. This is where we are. We meet the tools, we learn how to talk to an agent, and we go from an empty folder to working software without writing code. It ends with a commercial product, not a toy.

Week two is vibe engineering. That term comes from the writer Simon Willison, and it marks the shift from playing to working. We move into the command line, into Claude Code properly, and we cover the things that make this professional. Slash commands, checkpoints, M C P, skills, plugins, and long autonomous loops. By the end of that week you can raise a ticket in Jira and watch an agent pick it up, build it, test it, and push the change to GitHub.

Week three is agentic engineering as an expert, and it is where it gets genuinely strange. Sub agents. Teams of agents. Swarms and orchestrators. Ten agents working at once while you make coffee, running in sandboxes so they cannot hurt anything. We look at large existing codebases, which is where this technology still shows its rough edges most honestly. And it ends with a capstone that should make your jaw drop.
And to make that concrete, here is what you will have actually built by the end. Four things, all of them yours, all of them real.

A personal website with an A I version of you built into it, that can answer questions about your career. A project management platform, with a Kanban board and a database, that you can talk to in plain English. A software as a service product that drafts legal documents and hands you a P D F. And a real time trading workstation, with live market data and an assistant that can reason about strategy.

Four working products. Not four tutorials you followed and threw away. And by the end you will be able to go back to that post, the one we started with, and answer it. You will have held the alien tool. You will have read the manual. Tomorrow, we go and find out how the thing actually works.
